gettingStarted.title: Quick Start
gettingStarted.subtitle: Welcome to PantryButler! This guide will help you get started quickly and understand the basic concepts and usage.

whatIsKitchen.title: What is a Kitchen?
whatIsKitchen.description: A kitchen is an independent workspace containing all your recipes, meal plans, shopping lists, and pantry data. Each kitchen is completely isolated, suitable for different scenarios:
whatIsKitchen.familyKitchen: Family Kitchen: Share recipes and meal plans with family members
whatIsKitchen.personalKitchen: Personal Kitchen: Manage your personal cooking records
whatIsKitchen.teamKitchen: Team Kitchen: Collaborative use for culinary teams

step1.title: Step 1: Setup Your Kitchen
step1.description: First-time users need to create a new kitchen
items: Click the "Setup Kitchen" button on the homepage
Enter a kitchen name (e.g., My Family Kitchen)
Set up administrator account information (username and password)
Click "Create" to complete kitchen setup
step1.alert: The account created during kitchen setup will automatically become the administrator with full management permissions

step2.title: Step 2: Login to the System
step2.description: Use your created account to login
items: Click the "Login" button to access the login page
Enter your username and password
Select the kitchen you want to login to
Click "Login" to enter the system

step3.title: Step 3: Start Using
items: Create your first recipe
Plan this week's meals in the calendar
Generate shopping lists
Record pantry inventory
Invite family members to join the kitchen

navigation.title: System Navigation
navigation.description: After logging in, you can access all feature modules through the left navigation bar:

recipes.title: Recipes
recipes.description: Browse, create, and manage your recipe collection

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.description: Plan daily meals and view meal schedules

shoppingList.title: Shopping List
shoppingList.description: Manage shopping lists and track purchase progress

nextSteps.title: Next Steps
nextSteps.description: Now that you understand the basic concepts, continue reading the following documentation to learn more about each feature:
items: Kitchen Management: Learn how to manage kitchens and users
Recipe Management: Learn to create and organize recipes
Meal Planning: Master meal planning techniques
Shopping Lists: Efficiently manage the shopping process

instanceManagement.title: Kitchen Management
instanceManagement.subtitle: Learn how to create, configure, and manage your kitchens, as well as manage kitchen members and permissions.

creating.title: Creating a New Kitchen
creating.description: Creating a kitchen is the first step in using the system. Each kitchen is an independent workspace.

steps.title: Access Registration Page
steps.description: Click the "Setup Kitchen" button on the homepage

steps.title: Fill in Kitchen Information
steps.description: Enter a kitchen name, suggest using meaningful names like "Smith Family Kitchen" or "Culinary Studio"

steps.title: Set Up Administrator Account
steps.description: Create administrator username and password, this account will have full management permissions

steps.title: Complete Creation
steps.description: Click the "Create" button, the system will automatically initialize the kitchen and log you in

creating.alert: After kitchen creation, common ingredients and equipment data will be automatically initialized, and you can start using it immediately

userManagement.title: User Management
userManagement.description: Administrators can add, edit, and delete kitchen members, and control user permissions.

adding.title: Adding New Users
adding.description: Invite others to join your kitchen
steps: Go to the "User Management" page
Click the "Add User" button
Fill in username and initial password
Select user role (Administrator or Regular Member)
Click "Create" to complete the addition
adding.alert: After creating a new user, it's recommended to notify them to change their initial password

administrator.title: Administrator
permissions: Full system access permissions
Can add, edit, and delete users
Can manage all recipes and data
Can modify kitchen settings

member.title: Regular Member
permissions: Can create and manage their own recipes
Can view shared recipes within the kitchen
Can plan meals and create shopping lists
Can manage personal pantry data
Cannot manage other users

editing.title: Editing Users
steps: Find the target user in the user list
Click the "Edit" button
Modify username, password, or role
Save changes

deleting.title: Deleting Users
deleting.content: Click the "Delete" button in the user list to remove a user. After deletion, the user will no longer be able to access the kitchen.
deleting.alert: Deleting a user will not delete the recipes and data they created, which will remain in the kitchen

settings.title: Kitchen Settings
settings.description: Administrators can configure various kitchen parameters on the "Settings" page.
options: Kitchen Name: Modify the kitchen display name
Default Unit System: Choose metric or imperial units
Currency: select the currency used to display prices and costs
Cost Tracking: show estimated costs on recipe, calendar, and grocery pages

bestPractices.title: Best Practices
items: Choose clear, meaningful names for kitchens
Regularly review the user list and remove members who no longer need access
Create different kitchens for different purposes to maintain data isolation
Set up at least two administrator accounts to avoid single points of failure
Remind users to change passwords regularly to protect account security

mealPlanning.title: Meal Planning
mealPlanning.subtitle: Use the calendar feature to plan daily meals, making your diet more organized and your life more regular.

calendarView.title: Calendar View
calendarView.description: The calendar provides an intuitive time view to help you plan and view meal arrangements.
calendarView.viewModesDescription: Choose how many days the calendar shows at once

days7.title: 7 Days
days7.description: A compact week ahead for quick meal decisions

days14.title: 14 Days
days14.description: A two-week overview balancing variety and planning

days30.title: 30 Days
days30.description: A full month of meals for long-term planning

costTracking.title: Meal Cost
costTracking.description: When cost tracking is enabled, each planned meal shows its estimated cost, calculated from the recipe and your pantry prices.

addingMeals.title: Adding Meals
addingMeals.description: Schedule recipes in the calendar to plan daily meals.

steps.title: Select Date
steps.description: Click the target date in the calendar

steps.title: Choose Meal Time
steps.description: Select breakfast, lunch, dinner, or snack

steps.title: Add Recipe
steps.description: Select the dish to prepare from the recipe library

steps.title: Set Servings
steps.description: Adjust portions based on number of diners

steps.title: Add Notes
steps.description: Optional: Add special instructions or reminders

addingMeals.alert: One meal time can include multiple recipes, suitable for preparing multiple dishes

unscheduledRecipes.title: Unscheduled Recipes
unscheduledRecipes.description: See which recipes have not been planned yet
unscheduledRecipes.content: The calendar shows an "Unscheduled Recipes" list with dishes that are not scheduled anywhere in the current week. Use it to fill in empty meal slots or balance your weekly menu.

managingPlans.title: Managing Meal Plans
managingPlans.description: Flexibly adjust and optimize your meal arrangements.

edit.title: Edit Meals
steps: Click the meal item in the calendar
Modify recipe, servings, or notes
Save changes

delete.title: Delete Meals
delete.content: Click the meal item and select "Delete" to remove the meal arrangement.

shoppingIntegration.title: Integration with Shopping Lists
shoppingIntegration.description: Automatically generate shopping lists based on meal plans.
shoppingIntegration.generateDescription: Create shopping list with one click

steps.title: Select Time Range
steps.description: Choose the date range for shopping list generation, such as "This Week" or "Next Week"

steps.title: Auto-Aggregate Ingredients
steps.description: System will aggregate all ingredients needed for meals

steps.title: Deduct Inventory
steps.description: Automatically deduct ingredients already in pantry

steps.title: Generate List
steps.description: Create final shopping list, ready to use

shoppingIntegration.alert: Regularly updating pantry inventory makes shopping lists more accurate

bestPractices.title: Best Practices
items: Plan a week's meals in advance to avoid last-minute decisions
Consider nutritional balance, reasonably match different types of dishes
Schedule some quick meals for busy days
Leave flexibility, no need to strictly execute every day
Use weekends to prepare dishes that require long cooking times
Regularly review meal plans to summarize experience and preferences
Share calendar with family to understand each other's meal arrangements

groceryLists.title: Shopping Lists
groceryLists.subtitle: Intelligently generate and manage shopping lists, optimize the shopping process, and avoid omissions and duplicate purchases.

creating.title: Creating Shopping Lists
creating.description: The system provides multiple ways to create shopping lists to meet different scenario needs.

fromMealPlan.title: Generate from Meal Plan

steps.title: Go to Shopping List Creation Page
steps.description: Select "Shopping List" from the navigation bar

steps.title: Select Date Range
steps.description: Choose the time period for ingredient shopping, such as "This Week" or "Next Week"

steps.title: Select Recipes
steps.description: System will display all meals in that time period, can selectively add

steps.title: Auto-Aggregate
steps.description: System will merge same ingredients and calculate total quantities

steps.title: Deduct Inventory
steps.description: Automatically deduct ingredients already in pantry

steps.title: Generate List
steps.description: Create final shopping list

fromMealPlan.alert: System intelligently merges same ingredients, for example, if multiple recipes need "eggs", it will automatically calculate the total quantity

fromRecipe.title: Generate from Single Recipe
fromRecipe.description: Quickly create list for a single dish
steps: Open recipe details page
Click "Add to Shopping List" button
Select existing list or create new list
Set servings
Confirm addition

manual.title: Manual Creation
manual.content: Create blank shopping list and manually add items to purchase. Suitable for daily restocking or purchasing non-recipe related items.

managing.title: Managing Shopping Lists
managing.description: Update list status in real-time during shopping.

view.title: View List
view.intro: Shopping list organized by category, convenient for shopping by area in supermarket:

markPurchased.title: Mark as Purchased
markPurchased.content: While shopping, click the checkbox next to items to mark as purchased. Purchased items will show strikethrough but remain in the list for verification.

addCustom.title: Add Custom Items
addCustom.content: Click "Add Item" in the shopping list to manually enter other items to purchase, such as daily necessities, snacks, etc.

delete.title: Delete Items
delete.content: If an item doesn't need to be purchased (such as already at home), it can be directly deleted from the list.

costTracking.title: Estimated Cost
costTracking.description: Understand the total cost of your shopping list.
costTracking.content: When cost tracking is enabled, the list header shows an estimated total calculated from your pantry unit prices.
costTracking.purchasePrice: When adding a list item to your pantry, you can enter the price you paid, so future cost estimates stay accurate.

history.title: List History
history.description: View and manage historical shopping lists.
history.intro: System saves all created shopping lists, you can:
actions: Copy historical lists to create new lists

sharing.title: Share Lists
sharing.description: Share shopping lists with family to collaborate on shopping.
sharing.intro: Members of the same kitchen can jointly view and edit shopping lists:
features: One person creates list, other members can view
Anyone can mark items as purchased
Real-time sync updates to avoid duplicate purchases
Suitable for divided shopping scenarios
sharing.alert: Example: Mom creates list at home, Dad can view and update in real-time while shopping at supermarket

smartFeatures.title: Smart Features
smartFeatures.description: Use system's smart features to improve shopping efficiency.

unitConversion.title: Unit Conversion
unitConversion.content: System automatically converts and merges same ingredients with different units, such as "500g flour" and "1 lb flour" will be intelligently merged.

inventoryIntegration.title: Inventory Integration
inventoryIntegration.content: Automatically deduct pantry inventory when generating lists, can update pantry data with one click after shopping.

bestPractices.title: Best Practices
items: Regularly update pantry inventory to ensure shopping list accuracy
Create list one day in advance to have time for review and adjustment
Reorder items by supermarket layout to improve shopping efficiency
Add brand or specification notes to items to avoid buying wrong products
Mark purchased items promptly after shopping to keep list accurate
Keep historical lists to analyze shopping patterns and budget
Share lists with family to avoid duplicate shopping

pantryEquipment.title: Pantry & Equipment
pantryEquipment.subtitle: Manage ingredient inventory and kitchen equipment to optimize resource utilization and reduce waste.

pantryManagement.title: Pantry Management
pantryManagement.description: Track ingredient inventory, understand available resources, and avoid duplicate purchases.

addIngredients.title: Add Ingredients

steps.title: Go to Pantry Page
steps.description: Select "Pantry" from the navigation bar

steps.title: Click Add Button
steps.description: Select "Add Ingredient"

steps.title: Fill in Ingredient Information
steps.description: Enter ingredient name, quantity, unit

steps.title: Choose Storage Location
steps.description: Mark storage location, such as refrigerator, freezer, cabinet, etc.

addIngredients.alert: After shopping, you can import ingredients to pantry with one click from shopping list

ingredientFeatures.title: Ingredient Management Features
features: Sort ingredients by name or location, in ascending or descending order
Lists are paginated to keep the pantry easy to browse
Mark an ingredient as unlimited supply so it is never counted as out of stock
When deleting an ingredient or equipment, the system checks whether it is used by recipes and warns you first

manual.title: Manual Update
manual.description: After using ingredients, click ingredient item to reduce quantity or mark as used up

auto.title: Auto-Deduct
auto.description: When making recipes, system can automatically deduct ingredient quantities from pantry

costTracking.title: Track Prices
costTracking.description: Record purchase prices to unlock cost estimates across the app.
costTracking.content: Pantry ingredients support two optional price fields:

fields.label: Price Paid
fields.description: the total amount you paid for the item

fields.label: Price Covers
fields.description: the quantity that price applies to (for example, 500 for a 500 g package). Leave empty to use the item’s current quantity

costTracking.unitPrice: Unit price is calculated automatically and shown on each ingredient, making it easy to compare package sizes.

equipmentManagement.title: Equipment Management
equipmentManagement.description: Record and manage kitchen equipment, understand available tools, and choose suitable recipes.

addEquipment.title: Add Equipment

steps.title: Go to Equipment Page
steps.description: Select "Equipment" from the navigation bar

steps.title: Select Equipment Type
steps.description: Choose from preset list, such as wok, oven, blender, etc.

steps.title: Add Detailed Information
steps.description: Optional: Add brand, model, purchase date, etc.

steps.title: Set Status
steps.description: Mark as available, under repair, or damaged

addEquipment.alert: Common equipment will be automatically added when kitchen is created, you can adjust based on actual situation

recipeAssociation.title: Equipment and Recipe Association
recipeAssociation.description: Connect recipes with the equipment they need
recipeAssociation.intro: Equipment information links with recipe system:
features: Mark required equipment when creating recipes
Recipe pages list all the equipment needed to prepare the dish

maintenance.title: Maintenance Records
maintenance.content: Add maintenance records for equipment, such as cleaning, upkeep, repairs, etc., to extend equipment lifespan.

integration.title: Integration with Other Features
integration.description: Pantry and equipment data deeply integrate with other system features.

shoppingList.title: Shopping List Integration
features: Automatically deduct inventory when generating shopping lists
Import ingredients to pantry with one click after shopping

recipeRecommendations.title: Recipes You Can Make Now
features: The Recipes page highlights dishes you can prepare with your current pantry
Ingredients with insufficient stock are marked so you know what to shop for

mealPlanning.title: Meal Planning
features: Check pantry availability when scheduling meals
Warn about missing or insufficient ingredients
Automatically update inventory after meal completion

kitchenLayout.title: Kitchen Layout
kitchenLayout.description: Visualize your kitchen layout and organize ingredients and equipment by location for better inventory management.

createLayout.title: Create Kitchen Layout
createLayout.description: Design your kitchen layout with customizable elements

steps.title: Access Layout Editor
steps.description: Navigate to Pantry → Pantry Layout, then click 'Edit Layout'

steps.title: Create or Select Model
steps.description: Create a new kitchen model or select an existing one

steps.title: Set Canvas Size
steps.description: Define the dimensions of your kitchen layout canvas

steps.title: Save Layout
steps.description: Save your kitchen model for future use

addElements.title: Add Kitchen Elements
addElements.description: Drag and drop elements from the palette to build your kitchen
items: Upper Cabinet - Store dry goods and dishes
Lower Cabinet - Store pots, pans, and appliances
Countertop - Work surface area
Sink - Washing and prep area
Stove - Cooking area
Refrigerator - Cold storage (half height)
Freezer - Frozen storage (half height)
Door - Kitchen entrance/exit
Pantry - Dedicated storage space
Table - Dining or prep surface
Window - Natural light source

organizeItems.title: Organize Items by Location
organizeItems.description: Assign ingredients and equipment to specific kitchen elements

steps.title: Switch to Pantry Mode
steps.description: In Pantry Layout page, view your kitchen with items

steps.title: Drag Items to Elements
steps.description: Drag ingredients or equipment from the right panel onto kitchen elements

steps.title: Configure Shelves
steps.description: Right-click elements to add shelves and organize items vertically

steps.title: View Item Locations
steps.description: Click any element to see all items stored in that location

organizeItems.alert: Items assigned to kitchen elements will show their location as 'Model Name\Element Name' in the Ingredients and Equipment pages

features.title: Layout Features
items: Drag elements to reposition them
Resize elements by dragging corners and edges
Snap to grid for precise alignment
Rename elements with custom names
Customize element colors
Add multiple shelves to organize items
Delete elements with Delete key or context menu
Responsive canvas that fits your screen
Dark mode support with readable text

pantry.title: Pantry Management
items: Update pantry data promptly after shopping
Set minimum stock reminders for commonly used ingredients
Categorize by storage location for easy finding
Use "first in, first out" principle to manage ingredients

equipment.title: Equipment Management
items: Completely record all kitchen equipment
Update equipment status promptly
Regularly maintain and upkeep equipment
Mark required equipment for recipes
Choose suitable recipes based on equipment

recipeManagement.title: Recipe Management
recipeManagement.subtitle: Learn how to create, edit, organize, and share your recipe collection.

creating.title: Creating Recipes
creating.description: Create detailed recipe records containing ingredients, steps, nutritional information, and more.

basicInfo.title: Basic Information
basicInfo.description: Fill in the recipe's basic information

fields.label: Recipe Name
fields.description: A clear description of the dish

fields.label: Description
fields.description: Brief introduction to the recipe's characteristics and flavors

fields.label: Image
fields.description: Upload a photo of the finished dish

ingredientList.title: Ingredient List
ingredientList.description: Record required ingredients and quantities in detail

steps.title: Add Ingredients
steps.description: Click the "Add Ingredient" button and enter the ingredient name

steps.title: Set Quantities
steps.description: Enter quantity and unit, such as "200g", "2 pieces"

steps.title: Group Management
steps.description: Create groups like "Main Ingredients", "Seasonings", etc.

steps.title: Add Notes
steps.description: Add instructions for ingredients, like "diced", "room temperature"

ingredientList.alert: The system will automatically recognize common ingredients, and you can also add custom ingredients

cookingSteps.title: Cooking Steps
cookingSteps.description: Record detailed preparation process with timers and images
cookingSteps.intro: Clear step instructions help you and others better recreate the dish:
features: Add each step in order with detailed instructions
Use concise and clear language to describe operations
Mark key times and temperatures
Add images to steps to show expected results
Set timers for time-sensitive steps - never miss a critical moment
cookingSteps.alert: Step Timers: Add a timer duration to any step (e.g., "Bake for 25 minutes"). When cooking, click the timer button to start a countdown with audio notification when complete.

stepImages.title: Step Images
stepImages.description: Add visual guides to your cooking steps
stepImages.intro: Upload images for each step to show exactly how ingredients should look at different stages. This is especially helpful for techniques like "mix until combined" or "knead until smooth" where visual reference makes a big difference.
features: Click the image icon on any step to upload a photo
Images help show texture, color, and consistency
Particularly useful for baking and complex techniques

equipment.title: Required Equipment
equipment.description: Mark kitchen equipment needed for cooking
equipment.content: Select required equipment from the equipment list, such as wok, oven, blender, etc. This helps with advance preparation and checking equipment availability.

organizing.title: Organizing Recipes
organizing.description: Use folders and tags to efficiently manage your recipe collection.

folders.title: Folder Management
folders.description: Create folders to categorize and store recipes
features: Click "New Folder" on the recipes page
Enter folder name, such as "Home Cooking", "Holiday Menus"
Drag recipes into folders
Support creating subfolders to build hierarchical structure

tags.title: Tag System
tags.description: Use tags to quickly filter and find recipes
tags.intro: Tags are a flexible categorization method, one recipe can have multiple tags:
categories: Cuisine Tags: Chinese, Western, Japanese, Korean, etc.
Dietary Tags: Vegetarian, Low-Calorie, Gluten-Free, Keto, etc.
Occasion Tags: Quick Meals, Entertaining, Lunch Box, etc.
Flavor Tags: Spicy, Sweet, Sour, Salty, etc.

search.title: Search and Filter
search.description: Quickly find the recipes you need
features: Search recipes by name
Filter recipes by tags
Filter recipes by folder
Filter by maximum cooking time

cookable.title: Recipes You Can Make Now
cookable.description: See which dishes you can cook with your current pantry
cookable.content: The recipes page checks your pantry and shows a "Recipes You Can Make Now" section for dishes whose ingredients are all in stock. Optional ingredients are ignored, and pantry items marked as unlimited always count as available.

gridRecipes.title: Grid Recipes
gridRecipes.description: Structured recipes that reference your ingredients
gridRecipes.content: Grid recipes use a table-style layout where each step directly references the ingredient list, showing exactly which ingredients and quantities are used. Enable grid mode in the recipe editor and build steps that link to your ingredients.

editing.title: Editing and Deleting
editing.description: Update and manage your recipe content at any time.

edit.title: Edit Recipe
steps: Open the recipe details page
Click the "Edit" button
Modify any content that needs updating
Save changes
edit.alert: You can only edit recipes you created, administrators can edit all recipes

delete.title: Delete Recipe
delete.content: Click the "Delete" button on the recipe details page or in the list. Deletion is irreversible, please proceed with caution.

costTracking.title: Recipe Cost
costTracking.description: See how much a recipe costs to make.
costTracking.content: When cost tracking is enabled, the recipe page shows an "Estimated Cost" card with the cost per serving and cost per meal, plus a Cost column next to each ingredient. Prices are taken from your pantry items and are only visible to the recipe owner.

viewing.title: Viewing and Scaling
viewing.description: Adjust portions and display quantities in the units you prefer.

servingsScaling.title: Servings Scaling
servingsScaling.description: Cook for any number of diners
servingsScaling.content: Change the serving count on a recipe page and every ingredient quantity updates automatically. You can also adjust a single ingredient directly and all other quantities scale proportionally.

unitDisplay.title: Preferred Units
unitDisplay.description: Show quantities in your preferred unit system
unitDisplay.content: Toggle between your kitchen's preferred units and the recipe's original units. Quantities are converted automatically and the original measurement is shown alongside.

conversions.title: Unit Conversions
conversions.content: Open the conversion dialog for any ingredient to see available conversions and switch between equivalent units. Conversions are loaded for common ingredients and applied automatically when units differ.

importing.title: Import and Export
importing.description: Import recipes from multiple sources including Cooklang files, URLs, and public recipes.

cooklang.title: Import from Cooklang
cooklang.description: PantryButler is fully compatible with Cooklang, the open-source recipe markup language
steps: Click "Import from Cooklang" on the recipe editor page
Upload your .cook file or paste Cooklang text
Review the parsed recipe with ingredients, equipment, and instructions
Confirm import to add the recipe to your collection
cooklang.alert: Cooklang format preserves ingredient quantities, equipment, timers, and step-by-step instructions

url.title: Import from URL
url.description: Import recipes directly from recipe websites
steps: Click "Import from URL" on the recipe editor page
Paste the URL of the recipe webpage
The system will automatically extract recipe information
Review and edit the imported recipe as needed
Save to add the recipe to your collection

public.title: Import from Public Recipes
public.description: Browse and import recipes shared publicly by other users
steps: Visit a public recipe page via shared link
Click "Import to My Kitchen" button
Select which kitchen to import to
The recipe will be added to your collection with all details preserved

review.title: Review Imported Recipes
review.description: Map ingredients and verify details before saving
review.content: Before an import is saved, a review page shows the parsed ingredients and lets you match each item to your pantry or the nutrition database. Badges mark exact matches, similar matches, and new items so you can decide how each ingredient should be handled. Imported recipes carry a badge showing where they came from and how many times they have been re-imported.

export.title: Export Recipes
export.description: Save a recipe as a Cooklang file
export.content: Open any recipe and click "Export as Cooklang" to download a .cook file. The export keeps the recipe's ingredients, steps, timers, and equipment, so it can be shared or imported into any Cooklang-compatible app.

bestPractices.title: Best Practices
items: Use clear recipe names for easy searching and identification
Record ingredient quantities and steps in detail to ensure reproducibility
Upload high-quality finished dish photos to increase visual appeal
Use tags wisely to build a personal categorization system
Regularly organize folders to keep recipe library orderly
Add notes to frequently used recipes to record improvement suggestions

sharing.title: Sharing & Collaboration
sharing.subtitle: Share recipes with your household, collaborate on meal planning, and enjoy cooking together.

kitchenCollaboration.title: Kitchen Collaboration
kitchenCollaboration.description: Members of the same kitchen can share and collaboratively manage all data.

sharingScope.title: Sharing Scope
sharingScope.intro: All members within a kitchen share the following data:
sharingScope.alert: This design is suitable for family use, all members can jointly manage household meals and shopping

family.title: Family Collaboration
items: Mom plans this week's meals
Dad generates shopping list based on plan
Kids help shop at supermarket, marking purchased items in real-time
Whole family shares recipes, everyone can add favorite dishes

roommate.title: Roommate Collaboration
items: Jointly manage refrigerator inventory
Take turns planning and cooking
Share shopping lists
Share each other's specialty dishes

team.title: Team Collaboration
items: Culinary team shares menus
Collaborate on developing new dishes
Unified ingredient procurement management
Track equipment usage and maintenance

admin.title: Administrator Permissions
items: Manage kitchen members (add, edit, delete users)
Modify kitchen settings
Manage all recipes and data
Delete any content

member.title: Regular Member Permissions
items: View all shared content
Create and edit own recipes
Participate in meal planning and shopping lists
Update pantry and equipment information
Cannot manage other users

shareRecipes.title: Share Recipes
shareRecipes.description: Share your recipes via public links or export for backup.

generateLink.title: Generate Share Link
generateLink.intro: Generate recipe share link that can be sent to others through any method:
features: Copy link to share with anyone
Embed in blog or website - Use the public recipe URL in an iframe or link
generateLink.alert: Blog Embedding: Public recipe pages are designed to be embeddable. Simply use the public URL in an iframe or as a direct link in your blog posts. The recipe will display with full formatting, images, timers, and all details.

publicSharing.title: Public Recipe Sharing
publicSharing.description: Share recipes with anyone, even without an account
steps: Open the recipe you want to share
Click "Make Public" or toggle the public sharing option
A unique public URL will be generated
Anyone with the link can view the recipe without logging in
Public recipes can be imported by other PantryButler users
publicSharing.note: Public recipes display your username and kitchen name, helping build your culinary reputation.

visibility.title: Set Recipe Visibility
visibility.intro: When creating or editing recipes, you can set visibility:

options.label: Private
options.description: Only visible to you and your kitchen members (default)

options.label: Public
options.description: Anyone with the public link can view and import the recipe

notifications.title: Notification System
notifications.description: Stay informed about collaboration activities and sharing information.

types.title: Notification Types
items: Recipe share notifications
Meal plan update reminders
Shopping list change notifications
Kitchen member change notifications

kitchenCollaboration.title: Kitchen Collaboration
items: Clarify member responsibilities to avoid duplicate operations
Regularly communicate about meal plans and shopping arrangements
Update shared data promptly to keep information synchronized
Respect content created by others, delete cautiously
Set up multiple administrators reasonably to ensure orderly kitchen management

privacy.title: Privacy Protection
items: Set recipe visibility reasonably
Don't share content containing sensitive information
Regularly check your sharing settings

nutrition.title: Nutrition & Cost Tracking
nutrition.subtitle: Understand the nutritional value of your recipes and how much they cost to make.

overview.title: Overview
overview.description: PantryButler can display a full nutrition label for every recipe and estimate costs from the prices you record in your pantry.

what.title: What gets tracked
what.description: Nutrition and cost information is computed automatically from your recipes and pantry data.
features: Per-serving nutrition facts with % Daily Value
Estimated cost per serving and per meal on recipe pages
Meal costs shown on the calendar
Estimated totals on grocery lists
Unit prices on every pantry ingredient

enabling.title: Enabling Nutrition Information
enabling.description: Nutrition facts are turned on and off at the kitchen level by an administrator.
steps: Open the Settings page from the navigation
In the Display section, toggle the Nutrition Information switch on
Recipe and public recipe pages now show the Nutrition Facts label
enabling.alert: Nutrition is enabled by default and only administrators can change this setting.

matching.title: Matching Ingredients to Nutrition Data
matching.description: To estimate nutrition, ingredients must be matched with foods in the nutrition database.

steps.title: Open an ingredient
steps.description: Go to Pantry → Ingredients and edit the ingredient you want to match.

steps.title: Use Nutrition Match
steps.description: The Ingredient Search dialog shows suggested matches from the nutrition database.

steps.title: Accept the match
steps.description: Pick the closest food; the ingredient now shows a "Nutrition linked" indicator.

steps.title: Or add custom data
steps.description: If no food matches, use "Add Custom Nutrition Data" to enter values yourself.

custom.title: Custom Nutrition Data
custom.description: When an ingredient is not in the database, you can enter its values manually.

fields.label: Serving Size
fields.description: the serving size and unit your values apply to

fields.label: Macronutrients
fields.description: calories, protein, carbohydrates, and total fat

fields.label: Other Nutrients
fields.description: dietary fiber, total sugars, sodium, and cholesterol

custom.alert: All custom values are entered per serving size and scaled to your recipe automatically.

calculation.title: How Nutrition Is Calculated
calculation.description: Values are estimates produced by the server from the nutrition database.
items: Each matched ingredient is converted to grams using per-food conversion factors
Per-100g values from the database are scaled to the quantity in the recipe
All ingredients are summed and divided by the number of servings
The nutrition label shows both totals and per-serving values

nutritionFacts.title: The Nutrition Facts Label
nutritionFacts.description: When nutrition is enabled, recipe pages display a US-style FDA nutrition label.

label.title: What the label shows
label.description: A complete per-100g and per-serving breakdown
rows: Servings per recipe and serving size
Amount per serving with % Daily Value
Total Fat, Cholesterol, Sodium, Total Carbohydrate, Protein
Dietary Fiber, Total Sugars, and added micronutrients
label.alert: Nutrition data is provided by OpenNutrition and is an estimate based on ingredient matching.

costOverview.title: Cost Tracking
costOverview.description: Estimate how much your recipes, meals, and shopping lists cost using pantry prices.

where.title: Where costs appear
items: Recipe page — an Estimated Cost card with cost per serving and per meal
Meal calendar — a cost shown next to each planned meal
Grocery list — an Estimated Cost total in the list header
Ingredients page — a unit price on every priced item
where.alert: Recipe cost details are only visible to the recipe owner.

pantryPrices.title: Adding Prices to Pantry Items
pantryPrices.description: Costs are computed from the price fields on your pantry ingredients.

fields.title: Two optional price fields
fields.description: Available when adding or editing a pantry ingredient

list.label: Price
list.description: the total amount you paid for the item

list.label: Price covers
list.description: the quantity that price applies to, for example 500 for a 500 g package. Leave empty to use the current amount.

fields.unitPrice: Unit price is calculated automatically and shown on each ingredient so you can compare package sizes.

costSettings.title: Enabling Cost Tracking
costSettings.description: Cost tracking is turned on and off at the kitchen level by an administrator.

steps.title: Open Settings
steps.description: Open the Settings page from the navigation.

steps.title: Toggle Cost Tracking
steps.description: In the Display section, turn the Cost Tracking switch on.

steps.title: Choose a currency
steps.description: Select the currency used to display prices and costs from the list of supported currencies.

bestPractices.title: Best Practices
items: Match ingredients to the nutrition database for complete labels
Keep pantry prices up to date so estimates stay accurate
Record the price and the quantity it covers for packaged items
Enter the price you paid when moving purchased items into the pantry

account.title: Account, Settings & Announcements
account.subtitle: Manage your display name, password, personal preferences, and kitchen announcements.

profile.title: Your Profile
profile.description: The Profile page stores your personal information shown to other members.

info.title: Profile information

fields.label: Username
fields.description: your email address; it is your login and cannot be changed

fields.label: Display Name
fields.description: the name shown to other members of the kitchen

info.alert: Changes to your display name are saved immediately.

password.title: Changing Your Password
password.description: Keep your account secure by choosing a strong password.
steps: Open the Profile page
Click the Change Password button
Enter your current password, then the new password twice
Passwords must be at least 8 characters

kitchenSettings.title: Kitchen Settings
kitchenSettings.description: Kitchen-wide preferences controlled by an administrator, plus your personal language choice.

units.title: Preferred Unit System
units.description: Choose how quantities are displayed across the app

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: The currency used to display prices and costs
currency.content: Select the currency used for cost tracking from the list of supported currencies.

features.title: Display options
features.description: Settings that change how the app looks and behaves

options.label: Dark Mode
options.description: switch between light and dark themes

options.label: Nutrition Information
options.description: display nutrition facts on recipe pages

options.label: Cost Tracking
options.description: display estimated costs on recipe, calendar, and grocery pages

features.alert: Display options are kitchen settings controlled by an administrator; the language picker is personal.

language.title: Language
language.description: Choose the language used in the interface. This is a personal preference applied immediately.

rights.title: Data, Tokens & Tutorials
rights.description: Manage your data, create API tokens for integrations, and get help with tutorials.

apiTokens.title: API Tokens
apiTokens.description: Long-lived tokens for the browser extension and mobile apps
apiTokens.content: Create tokens with scoped permissions from the Settings → API Tokens card. Tokens are shown once at creation, so copy them somewhere safe.

data.title: Export & Backup
data.description: Own your data and keep it portable
items: Export all recipes as a Cooklang (.cook) archive
Import recipes from Cooklang files, URLs, and public recipes
Admin export of nutrition database data

tutorials.title: Tutorials
tutorials.description: Guided tutorials that introduce each feature
items: Follow step-by-step tutorials for every major feature
Track how many tutorials you have completed
Reset all tutorials from the Settings page to review them again

announcements.title: Announcements
announcements.description: Administrators post announcements to keep every kitchen member informed.

viewing.title: Viewing announcements
viewing.description: Announcements appear on the Announcements page
items: You are redirected to the Announcements page when there is something new
Unread announcements are highlighted in the notifications
Reading an announcement marks it as viewed

manage.title: Managing announcements
manage.description: Instance administrators can create announcements; superadmins can edit and delete them

steps.title: Open the Announcements page
steps.description: Go to Announcements and click New Announcement.

steps.title: Write the announcement
steps.description: Give it a title and a message, then publish.

steps.title: Edit or deactivate
steps.description: Superadmins can edit announcements and set them active or inactive.

bestPractices.title: Best Practices
items: Use a clear display name so other members recognize you
Keep an eye on announcements for important kitchen updates
Create API tokens with the minimum permissions you need
Back up your recipes regularly with Export

api.title: API Guidelines
api.subtitle: Authenticate against the PantryButler API with tokens or OAuth2, request scoped permissions, and integrate your own clients.

overview.title: Overview
overview.description: The PantryButler API exposes resources over HTTPS and accepts JSON. Every request must be authenticated.

options.label: API Tokens
options.description: long-lived tokens minted by a member for programmatic access

options.label: OAuth2
options.description: Authorization Code flow with PKCE for interactive apps

apiTokens.title: API Tokens
apiTokens.description: API tokens are long-lived credentials created by a member inside the app.

properties.title: Token properties
properties.description: What every API token looks like

items.label: Format
items.description: 32 bytes of base64url-encoded entropy, prefixed with pb_

items.label: Storage
items.description: only a SHA-256 hash of the token is stored on the server

items.label: Plaintext
items.description: the raw token is returned a single time at creation

items.label: Expires
items.description: tokens use a preset lifetime — never, 7, 30, or 90 days — capped at one year

create.title: Creating a Token
create.description: Tokens are created from the Settings → API Tokens card

steps.title: Name the token
steps.description: Give it a name between 1 and 100 characters.

steps.title: Choose scopes
steps.description: Select the permissions the token needs, or pick all for full access.

steps.title: Set an expiry
steps.description: Optional — choose a preset lifetime for the token.

steps.title: Copy the plaintext
steps.description: The plaintext token is shown once and never again, so store it safely.

create.alert: API tokens are shown exactly once at creation. If you lose the plaintext, revoke the token and mint a new one.

scopes.title: Scopes
scopes.description: Scopes limit what a token can do on your instance.
scopes.intro: Scopes are grouped into resources that each support read and write:
resources: kitchen — equipment and kitchen layout read/write
scopes.readWrite: You can also request a single all scope for full access:
all: all — every permission on this instance

revoke.title: Revoking Tokens
revoke.description: You can revoke access at any time from the Settings page.
items: Revoke a single token from the token list
Revoke every token on the instance with one action
A revoked token stops working immediately

oauth.title: OAuth2 with PKCE
oauth.description: Bundled clients — the browser extension and mobile apps — sign in with the OAuth2 Authorization Code flow using PKCE.

flow.title: Flow facts
flow.description: Requirements enforced by the authorization server
items: code_challenge may be 43–128 characters
code_challenge_method must be the literal value S256
The extension and mobile clients are pre-registered with the server
Development clients are enabled through the oauthDevClients server configuration
flow.alert: The PKCE S256 method is required; no other code_challenge_method values are accepted.

bestPractices.title: Best Practices
items: Request the minimum scopes your integration needs
Store tokens securely and never log them
Use a short expiry for tokens in long-running processes
Prefer the OAuth2 flow for interactive, user-facing apps
Include the token as a Bearer token in the Authorization header

access.title: Admin Features
access.subtitle: Server-wide and kitchen-level tools for superadmins and instance administrators.

enable.title: Enabling Admin Features
enable.description: Server-wide admin features are gated behind a configuration flag.

env.title: ENABLE_ADMIN_FEATURES
env.content: Set ENABLE_ADMIN_FEATURES=true in the server environment to expose the Admin pages and the admin API.
env.alert: While disabled, admin endpoints return an access-denied error and the Admin nav items stay hidden.

emailVerification.title: Email Verification & SMTP
emailVerification.description: With admin features enabled, new creators verify their email address before they can sign in.

behavior.title: How it works
behavior.description: The requirement is managed by the superadmin from Admin → Configuration.
items: While admin features are disabled, registration works as before with no verification step
With admin features enabled, verification is required by default (overridable via the REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION env variable)
The kitchen is created only after the email is confirmed
Verification links expire after 24 hours and can be resent

smtp.title: SMTP configuration
smtp.description: SMTP details are set by the superadmin from Admin → Configuration, falling back to environment variables.
smtp.env: SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USERNAME, SMTP_PASSWORD, SMTP_FROM and SMTP_SECURE control the mail server.
smtp.alert: Without an SMTP host, verification emails are logged to the server console instead of being delivered — configure one before inviting real users.

roles.title: User Roles
roles.description: Users hold either a server-wide role or a kitchen-level role.

superadmin.title: Superadmin
superadmin.description: The first account created during setup becomes the superadmin and can manage every instance.
permissions: View and delete any instance
Create, edit, and delete announcements for any kitchen
Manage the nutrition database
Access the Admin pages (when admin features are enabled)

instanceAdmin.title: Instance Administrator
instanceAdmin.description: An administrator of a single kitchen.
permissions: Add, edit, and delete kitchen members
Change kitchen settings
Create announcements for the kitchen
Manage all recipes and data in the kitchen

member.title: Member
member.description: A regular user of one kitchen.
permissions: Create and manage their own recipes
View shared kitchen content
Plan meals and create shopping lists
Manage personal pantry data

instances.title: Instance Management
instances.description: Superadmins can inspect every kitchen instance and delete abandoned ones.

view.title: Browsing instances
view.description: The Admin Instances page lists every kitchen with its creator and activity

delete.title: Deleting an instance
delete.description: Deleting a kitchen removes all of its data permanently
delete.intro: The following data is deleted with the instance:
delete.alert: Deleting an instance cannot be undone. Export anything you want to keep first.

announcements.title: Announcement Management
announcements.description: Announcements keep every member of a kitchen informed about updates.

manage.title: Managing announcements
manage.description: Available to instance administrators and superadmins
features: Create announcements with a title and message
Edit an announcement after it is published
Set an announcement active or inactive to show or hide it
Delete announcements permanently
manage.alert: Only superadmins can edit, deactivate, or delete announcements; instance admins create them.

bestPractices.title: Best Practices
items: Set up at least two superadmin accounts to avoid a single point of failure
Enable admin features only when you need them
Review instance activity and clean up abandoned kitchens
Post announcements for important kitchen-wide changes
